content.title: Golfer Gary Woodland Admits He's Struggling with PTSD During PGA Tour After Brain Surgery: 'I Feel Like I'm Dying'
content.text: The 2019 U.S. Open champ returned to the PGA Tour in 2024, months after he had a lesion on his brain removed Published on March 10, 2026 12:57PM EDT Gary Woodland. Credit : Richard Heathcote/Getty NEED TO KNOW Pro golfer Gary Woodland is sharing more about his recovery from brain surgeryThe 41-year-old had a lesion removed from his brain in September 2023Woodland, the 2019 U.S. Open winner, returned to the PGA Tour months later Gary Woodland is speaking out about suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following his 2023 brain surgery. In an interview with the Golf Channel, the pro golfer candidly disclosed his recent struggle to maintain his composure during tournaments. "Every week, I come out and everyone is so excited and happy that I'm back,” Woodland, 41, told the outlet. “I hear that every week: 'It's so nice to see you passed this. It's so nice to see you 100%,' And I appreciate that love and support, but inside, I feel like I'm dying.” He continued, “I feel like I'm living a lie. And I don't want to waste energy on that anymore. I want to focus my energy on me and my recovery, my dreams out here, my family. I don't want to waste energy hiding this." Woodland shared that he has been diagnosed with PTSD after his September 2023 surgery to remove a lesion on his brain. Gary Woodland. Orlando Ramirez/Getty After returning to the tour in 2024, Woodland — a fan favorite in the galleries — has been met with overwhelming support, but he recalled a recent experience in which he was triggered when a scorer in his group got too close for his comfort. "I stepped aside, I pulled my caddie and said, 'This stuff is hitting me, man. You can't let anybody get behind me,' " he said. "Next thing you know, I couldn't remember what I was doing. My eyesight started to get blurry. And a hole later, I just said, 'Butch, I can't handle it.' And I start bawling in the middle of the fairway. It was my turn to hit, and I couldn't hit." Related Stories The Kansas native and father of three — who has four PGA wins, including the 2019 U.S. Open — is now aiming to reset to a new normal following his health scare. This week, Woodland is in the field at the Players Championship at TPC Sawgrass in Ponte Vedra Beach, Fla. "Doctors have said in an ideal world, I'm probably not playing," Woodland said. "I'm probably not in a stressful, overstimulating environment. But my response was, in an ideal world, I don't have PTSD. [Golf] is my dream, this is what I'm going to do, and no matter how hard it is, I'm going to play."
